title: Air Flow Restriction / Air Leak Between Air Filter and MAF
plain: Air is either being blocked or leaking in between the air filter and the airflow (MAF) sensor. The engine may run lean or rough.

causes.name: Loose or cracked air filter housing or duct

checks: Inspect the air filter, housing and ducts
Smoke-test the intake for leaks
fix: Replace a clogged filter or repair the leak found.

cost.job: Find and repair intake air leak

title: Air Leak Between MAF and Throttle Body
plain: Air is leaking into the intake between the airflow (MAF) sensor and the throttle body, so it isn't being measured. The engine may run lean or rough.

causes.name: Cracked or loose intake duct or clamp

checks: Inspect the air filter, housing and ducts
Smoke-test the intake for leaks
fix: Replace a clogged filter or repair the leak found.

cost.job: Find and repair intake air leak

title: Air Leak Between Throttle Body and Intake Valves
plain: Air is leaking into the engine after the throttle body, such as from a vacuum hose or intake gasket. The engine may run lean or rough.
checks: Inspect the air filter, housing and ducts
Smoke-test the intake for leaks
fix: Replace a clogged filter or repair the leak found.

cost.job: Find and repair intake air leak

title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit
plain: The engine computer has found a problem in the circuit for the injection control pressure (ICP) sensor, which reads the high oil pressure used to fire the fuel injectors on some diesels. It usually points to wiring, a connector or the sensor itself.
checks: Inspect the ICP sensor connector and wiring for damage or corrosion
Check the sensor power, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the injection control pressure sensor.
examples: Used on oil-fired injection diesels such as the Ford Power Stroke 7.3L and 6.0L

title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The injection control pressure (ICP) sensor is giving readings that don't make sense compared with what the computer expects. This sensor reads the high oil pressure used to fire the fuel injectors on some diesels. The sensor may be failing or the system it watches may have a real problem.

causes.name: Failing or out-of-calibration injection control pressure sensor
A real fault in the system the sensor monitors
High resistance in the wiring or connector

checks: Compare the ICP sensor reading with related sensors in live data
Check wiring and connector for corrosion or looseness
fix: Confirm the system itself is working, then replace the injection control pressure sensor if its readings are off.
examples: Used on oil-fired injection diesels such as the Ford Power Stroke 7.3L and 6.0L

title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
plain: The signal from the injection control pressure (ICP) sensor is lower than the computer expects. This sensor reads the high oil pressure used to fire the fuel injectors on some diesels. A wire shorted to ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.

causes.name: Signal or reference wire shorted to ground

checks: Inspect the ICP sensor wiring for rubbed-through or pinched spots
Unplug the sensor and see if the reading changes, which helps separate wiring from sensor
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the injection control pressure sensor.
examples: Used on oil-fired injection diesels such as the Ford Power Stroke 7.3L and 6.0L

title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit High
plain: The signal from the injection control pressure (ICP) sensor is higher than the computer expects. This sensor reads the high oil pressure used to fire the fuel injectors on some diesels. An open (broken) wire, a bad ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.

causes.name: Open or broken signal or ground wire
Wire shorted to a power source

checks: Make sure the ICP sensor connector is fully plugged in and clean
Check the sensor ground and signal wire for an open circuit
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the injection control pressure sensor.
examples: Used on oil-fired injection diesels such as the Ford Power Stroke 7.3L and 6.0L

title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
plain: The signal from the injection control pressure (ICP) sensor keeps dropping out or jumping around. This sensor reads the high oil pressure used to fire the fuel injectors on some diesels. A loose connection or a damaged wire is the usual reason.

causes.name: Chafed wire that opens or shorts as the engine moves

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data for dropouts
Inspect the ICP sensor wiring along its whole route
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the injection control pressure sensor.
examples: Used on oil-fired injection diesels such as the Ford Power Stroke 7.3L and 6.0L

title: Injector Control Pressure Too High
plain: The oil pressure used to fire the diesel fuel injectors is higher than it should be.
checks: Check engine oil level and condition
Compare commanded and actual injection pressure in live data
fix: Repair the oil leak, regulator or sensor problem that testing points to.

cost.job: Replace injection pressure regulator or ICP sensor

examples: Seen on oil-fired injection diesels such as the Ford Power Stroke 7.3L and 6.0L

title: Injector Control Pressure Too High - Engine Off
plain: The computer sees injection oil pressure while the engine is off, which shouldn't happen. Usually the pressure sensor is giving a false reading.

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem at the ICP sensor

checks: Check engine oil level and condition
Compare commanded and actual injection pressure in live data
fix: Repair the oil leak, regulator or sensor problem that testing points to.

cost.job: Replace injection pressure regulator or ICP sensor

examples: Seen on oil-fired injection diesels such as the Ford Power Stroke 7.3L and 6.0L

title: Injector Control Pressure Too Low
plain: The oil pressure used to fire the diesel fuel injectors is lower than it should be.
symptoms: Low power, hard starting or stalling

causes.name: Leaking high-pressure oil system (seals or fittings)

checks: Check engine oil level and condition
Compare commanded and actual injection pressure in live data
fix: Repair the oil leak, regulator or sensor problem that testing points to.

cost.job: Replace injection pressure regulator or ICP sensor

examples: Seen on oil-fired injection diesels such as the Ford Power Stroke 7.3L and 6.0L

title: Injector Control Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking
plain: There isn't enough injection oil pressure while cranking for the injectors to fire, so the engine may not start.

causes.name: Leaking high-pressure oil system (seals or fittings)
Weak high-pressure oil pump or low engine oil

checks: Check engine oil level and condition
Compare commanded and actual injection pressure in live data
fix: Repair the oil leak, regulator or sensor problem that testing points to.

cost.job: Replace injection pressure regulator or ICP sensor

examples: Seen on oil-fired injection diesels such as the Ford Power Stroke 7.3L and 6.0L

title: Injector Control Pressure Erratic
plain: The injection oil pressure is jumping around instead of holding steady.
checks: Check engine oil level and condition
Compare commanded and actual injection pressure in live data
fix: Repair the oil leak, regulator or sensor problem that testing points to.

cost.job: Replace injection pressure regulator or ICP sensor

examples: Seen on oil-fired injection diesels such as the Ford Power Stroke 7.3L and 6.0L

title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Performance
plain: The second fuel pressure regulator isn't holding fuel pressure where the computer wants it. Fuel delivery may be too high or too low.

causes.name: Weak fuel pump or clogged fuel filter

checks: Compare actual and desired fuel pressure in live data
Check the low-pressure fuel supply
fix: Repair the fuel supply or replace the regulator as testing shows.

title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Control Circuit
plain: The engine computer can't properly control the fuel pressure regulator 2, which controls fuel pressure in a second fuel circuit, such as the high-pressure side on direct-injection engines. It sees an open or broken circuit, often from wiring, a connector or the part itself.

causes.name: Blown fuse or bad relay feeding the circuit

checks: Inspect the fuel pressure regulator connector and wiring
Check for power at the connector and measure the part's resistance
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the fuel pressure regulator 2.

title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Control Circuit Low
plain: The control circuit for the fuel pressure regulator 2 is reading low voltage. This part controls fuel pressure in a second fuel circuit, such as the high-pressure side on direct-injection engines. A wire shorted to ground or a shorted part is the usual reason.
checks: Check the fuel pressure regulator wiring for rubbed-through insulation
Measure the fuel pressure regulator resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the fuel pressure regulator 2.

title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Control Circuit High
plain: The control circuit for the fuel pressure regulator 2 is reading high voltage. This part controls fuel pressure in a second fuel circuit, such as the high-pressure side on direct-injection engines. A wire shorted to power, an open circuit or a failed part is the usual reason.

causes.name: Control wire shorted to a power source

checks: Check the fuel pressure regulator wiring for shorts to other wires
Measure the fuel pressure regulator resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the fuel pressure regulator 2.

title: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration Bank 1 Sensor 1
plain: When you lift off the gas, fuel is cut and the front oxygen sensor on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) should read very lean. It isn't, so the sensor may be slow or something is adding fuel.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
Possible small drop in fuel economy

causes.name: Slow or worn front oxygen sensor

checks: Watch the front O2 sensor during a coast-down in live data
Check for leaking injectors and exhaust leaks
fix: Repair any leak or fuel problem; otherwise replace the front oxygen sensor.

title: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration Bank 2 Sensor 1
plain: When you lift off the gas, fuel is cut and the front oxygen sensor on bank 2 (the side of the engine opposite cylinder 1) should read very lean. It isn't, so the sensor may be slow or something is adding fuel.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
Possible small drop in fuel economy

causes.name: Slow or worn front oxygen sensor

checks: Watch the front O2 sensor during a coast-down in live data
Check for leaking injectors and exhaust leaks
fix: Repair any leak or fuel problem; otherwise replace the front oxygen sensor.

title: Brake Pedal Position / Accelerator Pedal Position Incompatible
plain: The computer saw the brake and gas pedals pressed at the same time, or a sensor said they were. As a safety step it may cut engine power.
symptoms: Brake lights may stay on or not work

causes.name: Driver resting a foot on both pedals
Faulty or misadjusted brake light switch
Floor mat pressing the gas pedal

checks: Make sure floor mats aren't touching the pedals
Check that the brake lights work and turn off when released
fix: Adjust or replace the brake light switch if faulty and correct any pedal interference.
